1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 58:  p20.aspirate(4, cold_block["A1"]); p20.dispense(4, rxn_well)   # buffer
   The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the
     map verifies; the plate is the problem.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

   module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until
   `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), primers, rt and 1 more
   sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 108 times over the run. The
   person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3,
   A4 and A5 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 3.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 3, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.

   line 59:  p20.aspirate(1, cold_block["A2"]); p20.dispense(1, rxn_well)   # rt
   At line 59 the robot put rt into well A1 in slot 1. Take well A1 in slot 1: at that
   moment it held only 4 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line
   62, to make the 9 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in
   50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the
   buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry
   well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong
   places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to well A1 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then rt last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and
   hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html

           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: dntp (well A3 in slot 3)
findings.explanation: At line 60 the tip went into dntp (well A3 in slot 3) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 3) and rt (well A2 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 12 other wells: wells A3, B3, C3, D3, E2, E3, F2, F3 and 4 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 60 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 58 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 3, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), primers, rt and 1 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 108 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 3, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: rt
findings.explanation: At line 59 the robot put rt into well A1 in slot 1. Take well A1 in slot 1: at that moment it held only 4 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 62, to make the 9 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to well A1 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample, then rt last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: rt (well A2 in slot 3)
